issues.legal_issue: Construction alleged to breach court-imposed conditions does not constitute contempt when the structures were contemplated and permitted, served necessary functions, and did not materially encroach on the park.
material_facts: The applicants alleged that covered structures over staircases and a four-storeyed service building breached conditions imposed for construction of an underground market and prevented the park from being developed as a garden.
The structures appeared in the architect’s plan, were expressly permitted by the licence, and formed part of the sanctioned plan.
The covered structures were necessary for the underground market’s central air-conditioning, and the service building housed staff quarters while occupying less space than the earlier building.
The Court-appointed inquiry found no violation, and the Court agreed that the structures did not cover a substantial portion of the park.
issues.conclusion: There was no breach of the conditions imposed by the Court or the High Court, so no contempt was committed. The contempt applications were dismissed with costs.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, contempt was not established where the alleged conduct did not breach the applicable court-imposed conditions. In assessing breach, the Court considered the conditions laid down in its order and the High Court Division Bench’s order, together with the approved plans, licence, purpose and necessity of the structures, and the area they occupied. No earlier case was cited as authority.

rule.if: contempt_proceeding and structures_in_approved_plan and structures_permitted_by_licence and structures_serve_necessary_functions and not substantial_park_encroachment

predicates.contempt_proceeding: A party brought a proceeding alleging that conduct breached a court order.
predicates.structures_in_approved_plan: The disputed structures were included in a plan approved by the relevant authority.
predicates.structures_permitted_by_licence: The disputed structures were permitted by the applicable licence.
predicates.structures_serve_necessary_functions: The disputed structures served functions necessary to operate or maintain the project.
predicates.substantial_park_encroachment: The disputed structures occupied a substantial portion of the park.

issues.definition: When a contempt proceeding concerns structures included in an approved plan, permitted by a licence, serving necessary functions, and not substantially encroaching on the park, the rule means that contempt is not committed.

issues.legal_issue: Repeated, unfounded applications to prevent a development project are to be deprecated.
material_facts: The applicants had repeatedly moved the High Court and the Supreme Court alleging contempt in attempts to prevent completion of the underground market.
The Court found the allegations of breach unfounded and described the applications as attempts to hold up construction.
issues.conclusion: The Court deprecated the applicants’ repeated unfounded attempts to move the courts to prevent the construction.
issues.legal_principle: The Court expressly deprecated repeated attempts to invoke the courts on unfounded allegations in order to obstruct a development project; it cited no separate statutory provision or earlier case for this observation.

predicates.court_application_proceeding: A party made an application asking a court to act on an alleged legal wrong.
predicates.repeated_unfounded_applications: A party made multiple applications based on allegations the court found unfounded.
predicates.purpose_to_obstruct_project: The applications were made in an effort to prevent a project from proceeding.

issues.definition: When a party repeatedly makes unfounded court applications to prevent a project from proceeding, the rule means those applications are deprecated.
